extracted.intended_audience: advanced students and scholars of Kantian philosophy; translators of Kant; readers studying aesthetics and the Critique of Judgement
extracted.subtask_description: Understanding the aims, scope, and key terminological/translation conventions for Kant's Critique of Judgement (preface, introduction and glossary material). Useful for students, commentators, and translators engaging with Kantian aesthetics and the faculty of judgement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Principle of Judgement a priori
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the Judgement contains principles a priori peculiar to itself — i.e. principles that are not derived from concepts and that the Judgement must supply for its own right use.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text: "This principle must not be derived a priori from concepts, for these belong to the Understanding, and Judgement is only concerned with their application. It must, therefore, furnish of itself a concept, through which, properly speaking, no thing is cognised, but which only serves as a rule..." Use this as the central test for the Critique: identify a priori principles specific to Judgement and determine their character (subjective/objective).

rubrics_metrics.name: Constitutive vs. regulative status of Judgement's principles
rubrics_metrics.description: Determine whether the a priori principles of Judgement are constitutive (giving objective content to cognition) or merely regulative (serving as heuristic/regulating principles without claiming constitutive status).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Critique must decide "whether these are constitutive or merely regulative (thus indicating no special realm); and whether they give a rule a priori to the feeling of pleasure and pain..." Evaluate consequences for the scope of pure philosophy depending on that classification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scope of the Critique regarding aesthetical judgements (taste)
rubrics_metrics.description: Focus on aesthetical judgements (concerning the Beautiful and the Sublime) and their connection to the feeling of pleasure and pain and to cognitive faculties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The examination is ‘‘not planned in reference to the formation or the culture of taste ... but merely in a transcendental point of view.'’ The task is to establish transcendental principles for the faculty of taste, even if explanations are necessarily difficult or obscure; priority is given to correctly stating the principle rather than pedagogical cultivation of taste.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relation of Judgement to Understanding and Reason (division of faculties)
rubrics_metrics.description: Treat Judgement as a mediating faculty between Understanding (theoretical cognition) and Reason (practical cognition) and investigate how its principles a priori connect or differ from those of the other faculties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply the division: Philosophy divides into theoretical and practical; there are 'natural concepts' (theoretical) and 'concept of freedom' (practical). Judgement's role and its a priori principles should be analyzed in light of this division and its mediating function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transcendental method over pedagogical/cultural aims
rubrics_metrics.description: When analyzing taste and aesthetical judgement, prioritize transcendental-critical investigation (establishing principles a priori) rather than guidance aimed at cultivating taste or practical training.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Authorial caveat: the work is concerned with a transcendental point of view and may deliberately tolerate obscurities if the principle is correctly stated. Do not conflate critique of Judgement with taste-education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Translation convention: preserve consistent English equivalents for Kantian terms
rubrics_metrics.description: Render Kant's chief philosophical terms by the same English equivalents throughout to preserve exactness of expression, even at the expense of elegance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Text example: "I have tried to render them by the same English equivalents all through the work, in order to preserve, as far as may be, the exactness of expression in the original." The translator lists pairs to be distinguished (e.g. real ≠ wirklich; Anschauung ≠ Empfindung/Wahrnehmung; Vergnügen ≠ Lust). Follow the glossary list consistently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Typographic/lexical conventions for signalling Kantian distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use consistent typographic and lexical cues to mark philosophically significant German distinctions (e.g., capitalization or choice of English words to reflect German technical meanings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples from the text: "I have printed Judgement with a capital letter when it signifies the faculty, with a small initial when it signifies the act." Distinguish Objekt from Gegenstand by printing 'Object' with a capital initial when representing Objekt. Replace Kritik by Critique. Preserve Vorstellung as 'representation' to keep relation with vor-stellen. Maintain these signals throughout a translation/commentary to avoid collapsing Kant's fine verbal distinctions.
